{{Short description|Vietnamese mathematician (born 1970)}}
'''Lê Thị Thanh Nhàn''' (born March 23, 1970)<ref name="data">[http://www.tnu.edu.vn/sites/nhanltt/default.aspx Personal data for Lê Thị Thanh Nhàn] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160530045233/http://www.tnu.edu.vn/sites/nhanltt/default.aspx |date=2016-05-30 }}, [[Thái Nguyên University]], retrieved 2015-07-23.</ref> is a [[Vietnamese people|Vietnamese]] [[mathematician]] who is a professor of mathematics and vice rector for the College of Science at [[Thái Nguyên University]].<ref name="tnu">{{citation|url=http://www.tnu.edu.vn/en/Pages/female-faculty-of-thai-nguyen-university-accorded-kovalevskaia-award-tnund-516-tnunc-3-tnusite-36.html|title=Female Faculty of Thai Nguyen University accorded Kovalevskaia Award|date=April 21, 2012|publisher=[[Thái Nguyên University]]|access-date=July 24, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160305121244/http://www.tnu.edu.vn/en/Pages/female-faculty-of-thai-nguyen-university-accorded-kovalevskaia-award-tnund-516-tnunc-3-tnusite-36.html|archive-date=March 5, 2016|url-status=dead}}.</ref> Her research concerns [[commutative algebra]] and [[algebraic geometry]].<ref name="ictp"/>

== Biography ==
Nhàn's father was a soldier, who died when he was young, and her mother was a teacher. She was born in [[Thừa Thiên–Huế Province|Thừa Thiên–Huế]], and grew up in [[Thái Nguyên province|Thái Nguyên]] as the middle of five children in a poor family.<ref name="vnn">{{citation|url=http://vietnamnews.vn/sunday/features/222076/women-make-their-mark-in-sciences.html|title=Women make their mark in sciences|date=March 13, 2012|newspaper=[[Việt Nam News]]|first=Ha|last=Nguyen}}.</ref>

Planning to become a teacher herself,<ref name="vnn"/> she studied mathematics at the Thái Nguyên College of Education from 1986 to 1990, earning a bachelor's degree, and on graduating became a lecturer in mathematics at the same institution. She continued her education at the Hanoi University of Education, earning a master's degree in 1995 and then at the Institute of Mathematics, Vietnam Academy of Sciences and Technology, earning her Ph.D. in 2001,<ref name="data"/> under the joint supervision of Prof. Nguyen Tu Cuong and Marcel Morales of [[Joseph Fourier University]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|id=140559}}</ref>

She moved from the College of Education to the College of Science in 2002,<ref name="data"/> and was promoted to associate professor in 2005, becoming the youngest mathematician in Vietnam with that rank.<ref name="sggp">{{citation|url=http://www.saigon-gpdaily.com.vn/National/Society/2012/3/100128/|title=Vietnamese female scientists receive Kovalevskaia Award|author=B. Quyen, translated by Kim Khanh|date=March 4, 2012|newspaper=[[Sài Gòn Giải Phóng]]|access-date=2015-07-24|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150925091306/http://www.saigon-gpdaily.com.vn/National/Society/2012/3/100128/|archive-date=2015-09-25|url-status=dead}}.</ref> She has also been associated with the [[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]] in Italy as a junior associate member from 2002 to 2007 and as a regular associate member from 2009 to 2014.<ref name="data"/><ref name="ictp">{{citation|url=http://www.ictp.it/about-ictp/media-centre/news/news-archive/2012/6/prestigious-vietnamese-award-for-ictp-associate.aspx|work=News Highlights|title=Prestigious Vietnamese award for ICTP Associate: Le Thi Thanh Nhan is winner of the 2011 Kovalevskaia Prize|publisher=[[International Centre for Theoretical Physics]]|date=June 5, 2012}}.</ref> In 2009 she became vice rector.<ref name="data"/>

Nhàn was promoted to mathematics professor in 2015, becoming the second female mathematics professor in Vietnam (The first Vietnamese female mathematics professor in Vietnam is professor Hoàng Xuân Sính)

==Awards and honors==
In 2011, she was one of two winners of the Kovalevskaya Prize, an annual award to promote women in the sciences in Vietnam.<ref name="tnu"/><ref name="ictp"/><ref name="vnn"/><ref name="sggp"/>  The award is named after Russian mathematician [[Sofia Kovalevskaya]] and was established in 1985 by mathematician [[Neal Koblitz]] and his wife [[Ann Hibner Koblitz]], based on the profits from Ann Koblitz' biography of Kovalevskaya.<ref>{{citation | last = Hickey | first = Hannah | title=Neal Koblitz: Deciphering the cryptographer |url=http://www.washington.edu/news/2007/11/08/neal-koblitz-deciphering-the-cryptographer/ | publisher = University Week|date=2007-11-08}}</ref>
